section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that miracles clothed in nature, where the recipient does not recognize the miracle, are so natural that they are comprehensible to the intellect.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this matter
[that in miracles clothed in nature,
the essence of the miracle is in revelation]
is primarily regarding miracles where the recipient of the miracle does not recognize his miracle.
For miracles in which it is openly apparent that the garments of nature are merely a garment for the miracle that is clothed within them,
and even miracles in which it is not openly apparent that they are a miracle, but nevertheless it is apparent that they are something unusual
(like the four who are required to give thanks),
they are in the category of wonder that is not understood by the intellect
[therefore they are required to give thanks for them,
for thanksgiving (hoda'ah) is the nullification of the intellect25],
but miracles where the recipient of the miracle does not recognize his miracle are so clothed in nature that they are grasped by the intellect.
And based on this, it can be said that this—that the miracles drawn from the aspect of "Levado" (Alone) are in a manner that the recipient of the miracle does not recognize his miracle—
is,
because the matters drawn from the aspect of "Levado" are in revelation in every place
(for it is not possible that there be something that could conceal them),
and therefore they are clothed in nature in a manner that the recipient of the miracle does not recognize his miracle,
so that there is no wonder in them at all
(not even like the wonder of the four who are required to give thanks)
and they are grasped by the intellect26.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes the two types of miracles by their source: those clothed in nature come from Ein Sof's descent and revelation, while supernatural miracles come from Ein Sof's transcendence and concealment.
section.t: And behold, the distinction between the two types of miracles in their root is
(as explained in Shaar HaEmunah there27)
that the miracles clothed in nature, the source of their drawing down is from this—that Ein Sof is below, below, to no end28
—the matter of the spreading forth and revelation of Ein Sof,
which spreads forth and is revealed down to the lowest level29,
and therefore they come in revelation,
to the extent that they are grasped even by human intellect,
but the miracles that are above nature, the source of their drawing down is from this—that Ein Sof is above, above, without end28
—the matter of the concealment and elevation in Ein Sof,
which is elevated and concealed in concealment after concealment and in elevation after elevation,
above, above29,
and therefore,
even when they are drawn down below, they are above revelation,
wonders (nifla'ot).
And this is30
"As the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
that in the future redemption,
even the wonders whose source of drawing down is from this—that Ein Sof is above, above, without end—
will be in revelation,
and the revelation will be in a manner of seeing31,
"I will show him."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "I will show him wonders" in the future includes both greater wonders than at the Exodus, revealed continuously, and that these wonders will be clothed in nature while still being wonders.
section.t: And it can be said,
that in "I will show him wonders" that will be in the future,
there are two matters.
That even the miracles of the future that will not be clothed in nature
[like the splitting of the sea and the river—"And Hashem will dry up the tongue of the Sea of Egypt and wave His hand over the River etc."32]
will be in revelation,
similar to the miracle of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds that was at the Exodus from Egypt,
for although it was above nature, nevertheless they then saw in revelation
(not only the splitting of the sea,
but also)
the revelation through which the sea was split,
that each one pointed with his finger and said "This is my G-d and I will glorify Him"33.
And the innovation in "I will show him wonders" of the future relative to the revelation of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds is,
that the wonders that will be in the future will be wonders even relative to the wonders that were at the Exodus from Egypt,
that is,
that the wonders of the future will be drawn from a more elevated place than the wonders that were at the Exodus from Egypt34
[and therefore they will also be greater wonders in simple terms],
and nevertheless they will be in revelation and in a manner of seeing.
And also,
that the revelation that was at the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds was only temporary,
but the revelation of the future
(although it will be a more elevated revelation than the revelation that was at the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds,
nevertheless)
will be in a constant and eternal manner35.
And there is another matter in "I will show him wonders,"
that by means of the future revelation of the wonders to Israel,
their drawing down will also be in the world in a manner of revelation,
and therefore they will then be clothed in nature.
And nevertheless they will be wonders,
for this—that they will be clothed in nature—is not because they are in the category of revelation
[like the miracles clothed in nature now,
whose source of drawing down is from this—that Ein Sof is below, below,
the matter of the spreading forth and revelation of Ein Sof],
but rather,
that although the source of their drawing down is from this—that Ein Sof is above, above, without end,
the concealment that is above revelation
[and moreover,
that it is a concealment that is above even the category of revelation,
and as explained in the continuation of the Hilula36,
that this—that Ein Sof is above, above etc.—is that even in His Essence (Atzmus) He is not in the category of revelation],
nevertheless they will be clothed in nature,
for in the future, even the concealment
(that is above revelation)
will be in revelation.
